acceptance: The refusal's timing is established, and pr-arm waits (rather than refusing) for the full CI run of a just-readied PR whose only failed core is a placeholder, or the owner drops the item with the evidence.
context:
Filed 2026-11-22 while closing out the run-timeout follow-ups (umbrella run-timeout-plan-20261120). Evidence was read on 2026-11-22; re-read run logs, file paths and line numbers before acting.

Owner decisions 2026-11-22 (choice dialog): "Drop pr-arm item if not reproduced": one quick reproduction attempt; if pr-arm does not refuse a just-readied PR before its full run is listed, drop the item with the evidence.
description:
## Problem
On 2026-11-22 `make pr-arm PR=4443 HEAD=5c57945daf… WAIT=55`, run right after `gh pr ready 4443`, refused at once with "no verify-fast-duration verdict is recorded for 5c57945da: the core job ended failure for 5c57945da and no verdict will arrive; rerun it with make pr-rerun PR=4443, then arm again". The failed `core` came from the `CI (text edit)` placeholder run 45034069456 (attempts 1–3; `core` failed 14:42:06Z, 14:58:34Z, 15:20:16Z). The PR left draft at 15:05:16Z and the full CI run 45036340993 started at 15:05:18Z; that full run later failed on its own (`test (ubuntu-latest, 3.14)` and `core`), and the PR armed on a later head (4359467523). `_core_state` in `scripts/pr_arm.py` already treats a placeholder `core` failure as waiting while a full run is listed as not completed (#3598). So the refusal most likely came before the full run triggered by `ready_for_review` existed, or from a listing that missed a queued run. The invocation time was not recorded. Unproven: the advice to `make pr-rerun` a placeholder that a full run is about to replace wastes an agent's single rerun.

## Change
First establish when the refusal happened relative to 15:05:16Z and 15:05:18Z (the session's `make pr-arm` output time, or a reproduction: mark a draft with a failed placeholder ready and arm within seconds). If no full run existed yet, make pr-arm treat a just-readied PR with only placeholder runs as `waiting` for the full run; if a queued full run was not listed, fix the run listing.

## Decision gates
- STOP and record the finding if the timing shows the refusal was correct for the state GitHub returned and no reproduction exists; dropping the item is then the owner's decision.
- A failed `core` in a full CI run stays a refusal; do not relax any required check or the would-block duration rule.

## Verification rubric
Pass: the timing or a reproduction recorded on this item; a test with that shape (placeholder `core` failure, PR just readied, no or queued full run) yields `waiting`, failing before the fix; a test with a failed `core` in a completed full run still yields `refused` with the rerun advice; existing pr-arm tests pass.
Fail: change made without a reproduced cause.

## Guardrails
Work in a linked worktree (`make worktree-create`), never the primary clone. Edit files with the edit tool, never by script. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, UAT, generators at scale) only through `make heavy-run` or lock-taking entry points; never skip the lock, admission or watchdog; never delete anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. No live cloud run and no cloud credentials unless this item's Decision gates say the owner approved it in the current task. BenchBox imposes no default run limit: add none. No comments or docstrings in first-party code; one changelog fragment for a user-facing change. Never post a stand-in review, close and reopen a pull request to restart CI, use `--no-verify`, force-push, or rewrite an author. Arm once; a second time only after fixing the cause the refusal named. Reply on every review thread; resolve it only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise it again.
